title: P790 vs T200 vs Ai Smoke HL: Which Iron Set Fits Your Game?
excerpt: Compare three iron sets available from Karibu Golf: TaylorMade P790, Titleist T200 and Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team
cover_alt: Golf irons arranged for a Karibu Golf comparison guide in Kenya
seo_title: P790 vs T200 vs Ai Smoke HL Irons in Kenya
meta_description: Compare TaylorMade P790, Titleist T200 and Callaway Ai Smoke HL irons in Kenya by golfer type, launch, forgiveness, set makeup and price.
content:
**The short answer: choose the TaylorMade P790 or Titleist T200 if you want a compact players-distance shape, and start with the Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL if easy launch and forgiveness are the priority.** The correct choice still depends on your strike pattern, preferred flight, shaft and the exact set in stock. Karibu Golf currently lists all three models in Kenya: [TaylorMade P790](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/), [Titleist T200](/shop/product/gk-ir-ttt/) and [Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL](/shop/product/gk-ir004/).

This is a specification-led buying comparison, not a claim that one model wins for every player. We have used manufacturer information and the current Karibu listings. Ask for photographs and the precise shaft, flex, handedness and set composition before paying.

## Quick comparison

- **TaylorMade P790:** a hollow-body players-distance iron with a forged 4340M face in the 2025 model. It suits a golfer who wants a compact look with speed and useful forgiveness.
- **Titleist T200:** a players-distance iron with a forged face, hollow construction, Max Impact technology and a Tour-inspired profile. It suits a golfer who values a clean shape and controlled distance.
- **Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL:** a high-launch, deep-cavity game-improvement iron. Callaway says it is built for moderate-to-average swing speeds that need more launch to maximise carry.

Those categories are the biggest difference. P790 and T200 try to combine a refined head with distance technology. Ai Smoke HL starts from a more confidence-inspiring cavity-back shape and prioritises height and forgiveness.

## Which iron is easiest to launch?

On paper, the Ai Smoke HL is the clear starting point. “HL” means High Launch, and Callaway designed it with a low, deep centre of gravity, longer blade lengths and a deep cavity. Its 7-iron is 30 degrees. The manufacturer says its Ai Smart Face uses swing data to support launch, spin and distance across the face.

The P790 and T200 are not low-launch blades, but their compact visual profiles may suit a different buyer. TaylorMade describes the P790 as mid-high launching within its range. Titleist uses dense tungsten placement to tune launch through the T200 set. A player who already launches the ball high may prefer the visual and flight characteristics of one of these two, but a fitting is the best way to know.

## Which iron looks most compact?

P790 and T200 both target golfers who want a cleaner players-style appearance. TaylorMade gives the 2025 P790 a thinner topline and progressive leading edge. Titleist describes T200 as having less offset, an optimised blade length and a topline shaped from player feedback.

Ai Smoke HL has a longer blade and wider proportions than those two. That is intentional: the head is designed to look stable behind the ball and place mass where it can help launch. If a compact shape gives you confidence, compare P790 and T200 first. If a larger hitting area looks more reassuring, try Ai Smoke HL first.

## Distance versus stopping power

Do not compare distance using the number printed on the sole alone. Loft, club length, shaft, ball speed, launch and spin all matter. The reference 7-iron loft is 30 degrees on the 2025 P790, 30.5 degrees on the 2023 T200, and 30 degrees on the Ai Smoke HL. That puts the nominal lofts close, but it does not make their flight identical.

A useful comparison checks both carry distance and whether the shot lands at a playable angle. Ten extra metres is not automatically better if the ball cannot hold the green or leaves a large gap to the next club. Ask to compare carry, peak height, landing angle and left-to-right dispersion.

## Forgiveness and strike pattern

Forgiveness is not one universal number. A player who misses low on the face can benefit from a different sole or centre-of-gravity position than someone whose common miss is toward the toe.

The Ai Smoke HL is the most overtly game-improvement design here, with a deep cavity and a wider sole. P790 and T200 use hollow constructions and internal weighting to retain ball speed in smaller-looking heads. If your contact moves around the face, test your real misses rather than choosing from a centre-strike demonstration.

## Shaft, flex and total weight

The head name gets attention, but the shaft can change how the whole club feels. Steel is not automatically for strong players, and graphite is not only for seniors. Both are available in a range of weights and bend profiles.

A lighter graphite build may help some players create speed or reduce fatigue. A heavier steel build may give another player better tempo and face control. The labels Regular, Stiff and Senior are not perfectly standardised across manufacturers. Confirm the exact shaft model and weight, not only the flex letter. Read our [steel vs graphite iron-shaft guide](/blog/steel-vs-graphite-iron-shafts-kenya/) for the full checklist.

## Set makeup and wedge gaps

The current Karibu P790 listing is 4–PW. The T200 and Ai Smoke HL listings include 4–PW plus an approach wedge. Confirm every club physically included before paying.

The pitching wedge lofts also differ: 44 degrees in P790, 43 degrees in T200 and 43 degrees in Ai Smoke HL. The listed approach wedges are 48 degrees for T200 and 47 degrees for Ai Smoke HL. Check the loft of your next specialist wedge so you do not create an awkward scoring gap.

## Who should shortlist each model?

### TaylorMade P790

Shortlist P790 if you like a compact, modern players shape and want distance help without moving to a large cavity-back head. It is also the best-documented Karibu listing, with multiple product photographs and a detailed specification page.

### Titleist T200

Shortlist T200 if you want a clean Titleist profile, players-distance construction and a set that reaches from 4-iron to approach wedge. Pay particular attention to the installed shaft, because Titleist offers many different stock and custom profiles.

### Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL

Shortlist Ai Smoke HL if you need help launching the ball, prefer a more forgiving cavity-back shape or have a moderate swing speed. Confirm that the exact HL model is being quoted; Callaway also made standard Ai Smoke and Max Fast versions with different specifications.

## A five-step buying check

1. **Confirm the exact model and generation.** Similar model names can refer to different years.
2. **Confirm every included club.** Write down 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, PW and any approach wedge.
3. **Record the shaft.** Get the manufacturer, model, material, weight and flex.
4. **Check handedness and condition.** Request current photographs of the actual set.
5. **Compare the complete Kenya price.** Use the live Karibu price and confirm delivery or collection before payment.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is P790 more forgiving than T200?

Both are players-distance irons designed to add speed and forgiveness in a relatively compact head. Their forgiveness will feel different depending on where you strike the face, so neither is automatically more forgiving for every golfer.

### Is Ai Smoke HL only for beginners?

No. It is designed for golfers who benefit from higher launch and a confidence-inspiring cavity-back head. That can include improving players and experienced golfers with moderate swing speed.

### Which is best for a high-handicap golfer?

Ai Smoke HL is the logical first test because it is the most game-improvement-oriented model. Handicap alone is not enough to fit an iron, so also consider strike pattern, speed, launch and preferred head shape.

### Can I order these irons in Kenya?

Karibu Golf currently lists all three sets. Open each linked product page for the live KSh price and availability, then use WhatsApp to confirm the exact physical stock before payment.

content:
**The Titleist T200 is a players-distance iron for golfers who want a clean, compact profile with hollow-body speed and added forgiveness.** Karibu Golf’s current T200 listing is a 4–PW plus approach-wedge set. [View the live Titleist T200 listing, KSh price and availability](/shop/product/gk-ir-ttt/).

This guide uses Titleist’s 2023 T200 reference specifications and the current Karibu inventory record. Because model generations and custom shafts can differ, ask the team to confirm the markings, shaft and photographs of the exact set before paying.

## T200 buyer summary

- **Category:** players-distance iron.
- **Karibu set:** 4-iron through pitching wedge plus approach wedge.
- **Head design:** forged face with a hollow-body chassis.
- **Reference 7-iron loft:** 30.5 degrees.
- **Best reason to consider it:** a refined players shape with technology intended to protect ball speed and launch.
- **Main check:** exact model generation, shaft, flex, handedness and physical set composition.

## What kind of golfer is the T200 for?

T200 sits between a traditional compact players iron and a larger game-improvement iron. It is designed for the golfer who cares about how the club frames the ball but does not want to give up modern distance help. Titleist describes it as having a Tour-inspired shape, less offset, an optimised blade length and a topline informed by player feedback.

That does not mean it is only for low-handicap players. A confident improving golfer may like the shape, while a stronger player may use T200 in the long irons for extra launch. The question is not whether your handicap qualifies you. The better questions are whether you like the head at address, whether your common misses retain useful carry, and whether the sole suits your turf interaction.

## Forged face and Max Impact technology

Titleist says the T200 combines a dual-taper forged face with a reengineered chassis and refined Max Impact technology. Max Impact sits behind the face and is intended to support feel and performance across a broader area. The club is still a hollow-body construction, so “forged” does not mean it is built like a one-piece forged blade.

This distinction matters when comparing irons. The T200 aims to produce a solid sensation and controlled look while using multiple materials and internal design to add performance. Feel remains personal, and the ball, shaft and strike location also influence impact sound and sensation.

## Tungsten weighting and launch

Titleist uses dense D18 tungsten and an aerospace brazing process to position mass through the set. The stated goal is fast, high-launching long irons and more accurate, forgiving short irons. That progressive design is useful because a 4-iron and pitching wedge have very different jobs.

The reference T200 lofts are 21 degrees in the 4-iron, 24 in the 5, 27 in the 6, 30.5 in the 7, 34.5 in the 8, 38.5 in the 9, 43 in the pitching wedge and 48 in the approach wedge. Loft is only one part of flight; shaft, club length, strike and speed matter too.

## Sole design for real turf

Titleist says the T200’s variable-bounce sole was developed with input from its Tour players and Vokey Design. A softened trailing edge is intended to help the head move through the turf after contact.

For golfers in Kenya, turf can vary significantly between dry, firm conditions and softer conditions after rain. Your angle of attack matters as well. A shallow swinger and a steep swinger can react differently to the same sole. If possible, judge the club from real turf rather than a mat alone.

## Choosing the shaft

Titleist’s reference options cover a wide range of steel and graphite shafts. The official 2023 page lists steel profiles from lighter KBS Tour Lite through heavier Project X and AMT Tour White options, plus Mitsubishi Tensei graphite families. That range shows why “T200 with a stiff shaft” is not a complete specification.

Ask for five details: shaft brand, exact model, material, weight and flex. A 95-gram Stiff steel shaft can feel very different from a 120-gram Stiff. Graphite can also be built for low, mid or high launch; it is not simply the softer option.

## Does the T200 set cover the scoring clubs?

The Karibu listing includes 4–PW and AW. Based on Titleist’s 2023 reference lofts, the pitching wedge is 43 degrees and the approach wedge is 48 degrees. You should compare those lofts with the next wedge in your bag.

For example, jumping directly from a 48-degree approach wedge to a 56-degree sand wedge creates an eight-degree gap. That may be manageable for some players but large for others. Plan the bottom of the bag by loft and carry distance, not only by the letters stamped on the soles.

## T200 versus P790

Both the [Titleist T200](/shop/product/gk-ir-ttt/) and [TaylorMade P790](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) belong to the players-distance category. Both use compact-looking hollow-body construction. Their reference 7-iron lofts are close: 30.5 degrees for T200 and 30 degrees for the 2025 P790.

The most useful comparison is not a brand slogan. Look at address shape, sole interaction, shaft fit, carry consistency and the result from your normal miss. Our [P790 vs T200 vs Ai Smoke HL comparison](/blog/p790-vs-t200-vs-ai-smoke-hl-kenya/) explains where each model sits.

## Before you buy a T200 set

1. Ask for current photographs of the actual heads, faces, soles, shafts and grips.
2. Confirm the model generation against the markings and specification.
3. List every club included; do not rely on “full set.”
4. Confirm right- or left-handed build.
5. Record the exact shaft and flex.
6. Check the live price in Kenyan shillings and confirm delivery or collection.
7. Ask what happens if the supplied item does not match the written specification.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Titleist T200 irons blades?

No. They have a compact players-inspired shape, but Titleist builds them with a forged face, hollow-body chassis, Max Impact technology and tungsten weighting.

### Are T200 irons forgiving?

They are designed to be more forgiving than a traditional compact blade while maintaining a cleaner shape. A larger game-improvement head may still offer more visual confidence and help for some strike patterns.

### What clubs are in the Karibu T200 set?

The current listing is 4-iron through pitching wedge plus an approach wedge. Confirm all eight clubs with the team before payment.

### What handicap is suitable for T200?

There is no reliable single handicap cutoff. Strike pattern, speed, launch, preferred shape and shaft fit are more useful selection factors.

### Can I buy Titleist T200 irons in Kenya?

Yes. Karibu Golf currently lists a T200 set in stock. Use the product page for the live price, then confirm the exact set on WhatsApp before ordering.

Specifications above are manufacturer reference information for the 2023 model. The physical Karibu set should be checked separately before purchase.

title: Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL Irons in Kenya: Buyer’s Guide
excerpt: Who should play the high-launch Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL irons? See the specifications, set makeup and buying checks for Kenya.
author: Karibu Golf editorial team

seo_title: Callaway Ai Smoke HL Irons Kenya: Buyer’s Guide
meta_description: A Kenya buyer’s guide to Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL irons: high-launch design, 4–PW plus approach wedge, specifications, shafts and live stock.
content:
**The Callaway Paradym Ai Smoke HL is a game-improvement iron built for golfers who need help launching the ball higher and carrying it farther.** Callaway positions the HL model for moderate-to-average swing speeds. Karibu Golf currently lists a 4–PW plus approach-wedge set in Kenya. [See the live Ai Smoke HL price and stock](/shop/product/gk-ir004/).

This guide refers to the 2024 Paradym Ai Smoke HL specifications published by Callaway. Confirm the exact model, shaft, flex, handedness and photographs of the physical Karibu set before paying.

## Ai Smoke HL buyer summary

- **Category:** high-launch game-improvement iron.
- **Karibu set:** 4-iron through pitching wedge plus approach wedge.
- **Head design:** deep cavity back with a low, deep centre of gravity.
- **Reference 7-iron loft:** 30 degrees.
- **Best reason to consider it:** easier height and a confidence-inspiring head for moderate-to-average speed.
- **Main check:** make sure the set is the HL model, not standard Ai Smoke or Max Fast.

## What does HL mean?

HL means High Launch. It identifies a distinct model rather than a cosmetic variation. Callaway designed the head with a deep cavity, precision tungsten weighting, a low centre of gravity and longer blade lengths. Those decisions aim to help the ball launch on a higher trajectory.

This can be useful when shots come out too low to produce reliable carry or stop on a green. It can also help a player who wants a larger, more stable-looking head behind the ball. Higher launch is not automatically better for everyone, so players who already create excessive height should still compare flight.

## How the Ai Smart Face works

Callaway says it developed the Ai Smart Face from pre-impact information collected from thousands of golfers. The data included swing speed, delivery and face orientation. The HL face was then optimised around the launch and spin needs of its intended player.

That is the manufacturer’s design explanation, not a promise of a specific distance gain. Your ball speed, strike and shaft still determine the result. The practical test is whether off-centre strikes keep a useful carry and stay within a playable left-to-right window.

## Why are some clubs longer?

The 4- through 7-irons in the Ai Smoke HL reference set are half an inch longer than many conventional iron builds. Callaway says its face optimisation lets players use that additional length for speed while maintaining control. The 7-iron reference length is 37.5 inches.

Longer clubs can add speed, but they may also change posture and centre contact. Do not assume extra length is automatically helpful. Check whether you can find the middle of the face repeatedly and whether the lie angle suits your delivery.

## Loft and set specifications

Callaway lists the HL lofts as 21 degrees for the 4-iron, 24 for the 5, 27 for the 6, 30 for the 7, 34 for the 8, 38 for the 9, 43 for the pitching wedge and 47 for the approach wedge. The Karibu set is listed as 4–PW plus AW, which is eight clubs.

Those lofts create four- to five-degree steps through the set. The 47-degree approach wedge should then be matched to the next wedge in your bag. A 52-degree gap wedge is a common next reference point, but your actual carry gaps should decide the setup.

## Shaft options to confirm

Callaway’s original reference configurations include the True Temper Elevate MPH 85 in steel and Project X Cypher 2.0 60 in graphite. Those names indicate very different weight categories. The exact Karibu stock can vary, so do not assume the physical set has either shaft until it is confirmed.

Graphite may help a golfer who prefers lower total weight, wants help creating speed or finds a heavy build tiring. Steel may suit a golfer who likes more overall mass or a particular balance. Material is only one variable. Read the [steel vs graphite guide for Kenyan buyers](/blog/steel-vs-graphite-iron-shafts-kenya/) before choosing.

## Turf interaction

Callaway calls its sole a Dynamic Sole Design with a pre-worn leading edge and variable bounce. The aim is to move efficiently through the turf and maintain contact quality. A wider game-improvement sole can also help the head resist digging for some golfers.

Course conditions in Kenya are not identical everywhere or all year. Firm fairways, soft ground after rain, mats and range grass can each make the sole feel different. Try the club from the conditions you play most often if that is possible.

## Ai Smoke HL versus players-distance irons

The HL is visually and functionally different from compact players-distance models such as the [TaylorMade P790](/shop/product/gk-ir-tmp/) and [Titleist T200](/shop/product/gk-ir-ttt/). It has a deeper cavity, longer blade and more game-improvement-oriented proportions.

Choose from the job the club must do. If your priority is easy height and forgiveness, start with HL. If your priority is a compact profile with distance technology, compare P790 and T200. See all three side by side in our [P790 vs T200 vs Ai Smoke HL guide](/blog/p790-vs-t200-vs-ai-smoke-hl-kenya/).

## What to check before ordering

1. **The exact badge:** it should identify Paradym Ai Smoke HL.
2. **Set makeup:** confirm 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, PW and AW.
3. **Shaft:** record brand, model, material, weight and flex.
4. **Handedness:** verify right or left hand.
5. **Condition:** request current face, sole, cavity, shaft and grip photographs.
6. **Price:** use the live KSh amount and ask whether delivery is included.
7. **Fit:** compare launch, carry, landing angle and dispersion where possible.

## Frequently asked questions

### Who should use Callaway Ai Smoke HL irons?

They are designed for golfers with moderate-to-average swing speeds who need more launch. They can suit beginners or experienced players; speed, strike and preferred head shape matter more than a simple handicap label.

### Is Ai Smoke HL the same as standard Ai Smoke?

No. HL is a separate high-launch head with its own shape and loft specifications. Max Fast is another distinct version. Confirm the badge and model before buying.

### Are Ai Smoke HL irons forgiving?

Callaway designed them as game-improvement irons with a deep cavity, low centre of gravity and wider proportions. Those features are intended to support launch and off-centre performance, but individual results vary.

### What is included in the Karibu set?

The current listing is 4-iron through pitching wedge plus an approach wedge. Confirm all eight physical clubs before payment.

### Can I buy Ai Smoke HL irons in Kenya?

Yes. Karibu Golf currently lists a set in stock. Check the product page for live pricing and use WhatsApp to verify the exact specification.
